resale_co.name: Resale and/or Rental Certificate (Certificate of Continued Occupancy, CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Dumont Building Department (building and fire inspections)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are only on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 9:00 am and 11:00 am. The base fee assumes 11 or more business days' notice; shorter notice costs more. Open permits must be closed before the resale inspection.
requirements: All open permits must be inspected and closed before the resale inspection; no unpaid fees or property maintenance violations
Furnace/boiler flue connections properly sealed at the chimney
Water heater and mechanical equipment replaced under a permit, with an inspection sticker on the unit
Sump pump must discharge outside, not into the sanitary sewer
Anti-tip brackets on kitchen stoves where the maker requires them; rigid exhaust ducts for visible hood/microwave ducts where required
Electrical outlets, switches, boxes and panels covered; no lamp cords on fixed appliances
Handrails on 4 or more risers; guards on landings 30 inches above floor or grade and on open basement stairs
Garage walls and ceilings next to the house must be sheet-rocked
Pool fences and gates compliant (gates swing out, self-close and latch, latch 54 inches above grade); hot tubs need approved latches
Bedroom and bathroom count must match the property tax record
Smoke alarm on every level, less than 10 years old, 10-year sealed battery or hardwired
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of every bedroom (battery or plug-in)
For a 1 or 2 family resale, the buyer signs a notarized basement/attic use agreement (no separate dwelling unit, no bedrooms or cooking in the basement or attic)
Someone over 18 must be home for the inspection window

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Borough's Resale and/or Rental Certificate Application completely (single or two family, closing date, buyer and seller, room counts, open permits) and submit it to the Building Department, 50 Washington Avenue, with a check payable to the Borough of Dumont. One payment covers both the building and the fire (smoke/CO) inspections. The Building Department then schedules the inspection for a Tuesday or Thursday morning. Check for open permits first (openpermitinquiry@dumontboro.org).

evidence.quote: Please make checks payable to the Borough of Dumont. Payments include both Building and Fire inspections.
Are there any open permits on the property? If so, these permits must be inspected and closed prior to the Resale/Rental inspections.
One smoke detector on every level, mounted on the wall or ceiling as per the manufacturer instructions
Certificate of continued occupancy (CCO) for the sale of property:

resale_co.notes: The Borough's current application (posted July 28, 2026) is a combined Resale and/or Rental Certificate covering building and fire (smoke/CO) inspections for one fee. The Borough code fee schedule (Chapter 182, Section 182-2, last amended May 6, 2025 by Ord. No. 1653, read through the ecode360 print view) lists lower CCO fees ($75 one-family, $85 two-family, extra $25 or $100 for short notice) plus a separate $50 smoke detector certificate payable to the Fire Prevention Bureau; the form's higher fees ($125/$135) appear to be the current combined charge. No code section stating the resale requirement itself was found, but the fee schedule and the Borough's own application treat the CCO as required for sales. The construction official's direct line on the Building Department page is 201-387-5028. Rental-only items (lead-safe inspections for rentals, landlord matters) are not resale requirements. The Borough's main website is dumontnj.gov; older dumontboro.org/.com domains did not load.

requirements: Smoke alarm on every level, less than 10 years old, with a 10-year sealed battery or hardwired
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of every bedroom (battery or plug-in accepted)
Is the alarm system monitored? (asked on the application)

fire_cert.notes: Dumont is a municipal (M) fire code enforcing agency. The smoke/CO check for a sale is folded into the Building Department's combined resale certificate, so there is no separate fire application on the Borough site. The code fee schedule still lists a separate $50 smoke detector compliance certificate payable to the Fire Prevention Bureau; confirm which applies. The current form does not mention a fire extinguisher (consistent with P.L.2025, c.19). The state directory lists the fire official at (201) 310-1482 and a second number (201) 387-5041.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: All open permits must be inspected and closed before the resale inspection. Questions about older permits: openpermitinquiry@dumontboro.org.

other_items.label: Basement/attic use agreement
other_items.detail: For a 1 or 2 family resale the new owner signs a notarized agreement that the basement or attic will not be used as a separate dwelling unit, for bedrooms, or for cooking.

other_items.label: Sump pump
other_items.detail: Sump pumps must discharge outside and cannot be connected to the sanitary sewer; checked during the resale inspection.

open_questions: Which fee applies today: the application's $125 (single family) / $135 (two family) combined fee, or the code's $75 / $85 CCO plus $50 smoke certificate?
